entries.originalText: Avoid as far as thou canst the tumult of men; for talk concerning worldly things, though it be innocently undertaken, is a hindrance, so quickly are we led captive and defiled by vanity.
entries.modernizedText: Avoid the tumult of people as far as you can, for talk about worldly things, even when innocently undertaken, is a hindrance, so quickly are we led captive and defiled by vanity.

entries.originalText: Many a time I wish that I had held my peace, and had not gone amongst men.
entries.modernizedText: Many times I wish that I had held my peace and had not gone among people.

entries.originalText: But why do we talk and gossip so continually, seeing that we so rarely resume our silence without some hurt done to our conscience?
entries.modernizedText: But why do we talk and gossip so continually, seeing that we so rarely return to silence without some injury to our conscience?

entries.originalText: We like talking so much because we hope by our conversations to gain some mutual comfort, and because we seek to refresh our wearied spirits by variety of thoughts.
entries.modernizedText: We like talking so much because we hope to gain some mutual comfort by our conversations, and because we seek to refresh our weary spirits with a variety of thoughts.

entries.originalText: And we very willingly talk and think of those things which we love or desire, or else of those which we most dislike.
entries.modernizedText: And we very willingly talk and think of the things we love or desire, or else of those we most dislike.

entries.originalText: But alas! it is often to no purpose and in vain.
entries.modernizedText: But alas! It is often purposeless and vain.

entries.originalText: For this outward consolation is no small hindrance to the inner comfort which cometh from God.
entries.modernizedText: For this outward consolation is no small hindrance to the inner comfort that comes from God.

entries.originalText: Therefore must we watch and pray that time pass not idly away.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore, we must watch and pray so that time does not pass idly away.

entries.originalText: If it be right and desirable for thee to speak, speak things which are to edification.
entries.modernizedText: If it is right and desirable for you to speak, speak things that edify.

entries.originalText: Evil custom and neglect of our real profit tend much to make us heedless of watching over our lips.
entries.modernizedText: Evil custom and neglect of our real benefit do much to make us careless about guarding our lips.

entries.originalText: Nevertheless, devout conversation on spiritual things helpeth not a little to spiritual progress, most of all where those of kindred mind and spirit find their ground of fellowship in God.
entries.modernizedText: Nevertheless, devout conversation about spiritual things helps spiritual progress considerably, especially where those of kindred mind and spirit find the ground of their fellowship in God.
